document_metadata.summary: Midwife Emilie Wagner interacts with her son Hans, a boy with Down syndrome, who sings at school; children then leave, with some running ahead while Marie and others walk, followed by the camera.

document_metadata.summary: The steward and landowner examine a nearly invisible wire tied at knee height, suspecting it was intentionally placed, possibly to cause harm, though the reason remains unclear.

entities.description: The steward informs the landowner that the doctor was severely injured, with a broken collarbone, and was unable to speak about the incident involving the dead horse.

entities.description: The steward recounts that he asked the doctor's daughter about how the horse came to be injured, but she had no information to provide.

The landowner's overseer directs farmhands, while an estate official assigns search areas. A father seeks help for his ill baby, discussing the open window with the doctor.

document_metadata.summary: Franz confronts the farmer about his mother's death, implying negligence by the landowner; the farmer reacts angrily, dismisses Franz, and storms off, followed by others, while Paul silently observes.

entities.description: After a prolonged silence, the farmer finally replies to Franz with hostility, dismissing his concern and showing resistance to engaging with the issue.

entities.summary: A 13-year-old girl behaves maturely, showing concern for the doctor and offering to help care for Xenia; she is part of a group of children involved in community events, receives corporal punishment, is comforted by the pastor, and wears a white ribbon during the Reformation Feast before leaving the manor.

entities.name: Martin
entities.description: A child among the group leaving the manor, wearing a white ribbon.
entities.summary: A tall, gangly 12-year-old boy in elegant clothes, one of the oldest children, returns home late with Marie, walks dangerously on a bridge, confronts the schoolteacher, receives corporal punishment, and is seen leaving the manor wearing a white ribbon.

entities.name: Hansi
entities.description: One of the children in the group heading toward the open fields.
entities.summary: The midwife's mentally disabled son stays at school after lessons, plays with Rudolph, and is part of a group heading to the fields during the investigation.

entities.name: Liesl
entities.description: One of the children in the group leaving the manor.
entities.summary: A 15-year-old girl, daughter of the steward, is caring, plain, and anxious about her newborn sibling; she observes fires with other children, shares a troubling dream with the schoolteacher, and expresses fear it may come true.

entities.name: Georg
entities.description: One of the children in the group passing through the vegetable garden.
entities.summary: A group of children, including a 13-year-old boy who initiates races and a 10-year-old steward's son, interact during estate activities; the steward engages in teasing talk about motherhood, while one child retrieves the doctor's coat and another throws stones to get Xenia's attention.

entities.name: Ferdinand
entities.description: One of the children in the group heading into the open fields.
entities.summary: A 10-year-old boy, part of a group of children, awaits news of a newborn sibling, participates in outdoor activities, observes flames from a window, interacts familiarly with Sigi, and shows a competitive attitude while carving whistles with others.

entities.name: Siegmund
entities.description: One of the children in the group leaving the manor.
entities.summary: The Baron's son, a 9-year-old boy, disappeared after the feast with a group of children; one was found abused in a sawmill, while another, previously unwell, has improved in health, raising concerns about harm similar to past events.

document_metadata.summary: A farmhand whispers about the boy's mother's accident; a boy interrupts to report the Baron's cabbages being cut, shocking Leni as she serves drinks amid the raucous gathering.

entities.name: First tenant farmer recounts story about man attempting to steal rooster from steeple
entities.description: A tenant farmer tells a partially audible story about a drunken man who tried to climb a church steeple to steal a rooster, reached only the first window, failed to climb further, and began crowing like a rooster, waking neighbors.

entities.description: Farmhands and tenant farmers repeatedly shout for more beer, threatening to fall down and joking about the landlord hanging himself, creating a raucous and disruptive atmosphere.

entities.description: Leni, Franz's sister, and a fellow farmgirl work quickly to serve beer to the demanding and rowdy guests, struggling to maintain composure amid the chaos.

entities.description: Several farmhands tease Leni with suggestive comments and grins, offering mock help and making inappropriate remarks about her work pace and interactions with the Baron, provoking laughter.

entities.description: A second tenant farmer tells the others to leave Leni alone, attempting to curb the escalating verbal abuse she is enduring from the farmhands.

document_metadata.summary: The Baron urges villagers to help identify those behind his son's and the doctor's attacks, warning of lost peace if the culprits remain unpunished; the crowd exits anxiously, discussing the plea.

document_metadata.title: 47 RECTORY. THE BOYS' BEDROOM. INT/NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: The mother reassures the children about a fire on the estate, orders them back to bed, and has Anton retie Martin before they all settle down as the fire's glow remains visible outside.

entities.name: Martin awakens Anton to report a red glow outside
entities.description: Martin calls out to Anton in the dark, urging him to wake up and look at the intensifying red glow visible through the window.

entities.name: Anton observes the red glow and realizes something is burning
entities.description: After sitting up and rubbing his eyes, Anton turns to the window, sees the red glow, gets out of bed, and exclaims that something is burning at the estate.

entities.name: Martin demands to be untied amid growing urgency
entities.description: With increasing agitation, Martin repeatedly orders Anton to untie him, threatening violence if he is not released immediately.

entities.description: Disturbed by the shouting, Florian wakes up, questions the noise, and is told by Martin to untie him while informing him that a fire has broken out.

entities.name: Florian confirms the fire and expresses amazement
entities.description: Florian gets out of bed, goes to the window, sees the fire, and reacts with a mix of astonishment and excitement, confirming that the estate is on fire.

entities.name: Anton hesitates but ultimately unties Martin under pressure
entities.description: After internal conflict and being threatened by Martin, Anton decides to untie Martin's restraints despite uncertainty and fear.

entities.description: While still tied, Martin yells loudly for his father and mother, screaming that there is an emergency and someone must warn them about the fire.

entities.description: Responding to the shouting and footsteps in the corridor, the mother opens the door and enters the room wearing a nightgown, demanding to know what is happening.

document_metadata.title: 56 SCHOOL. INT/DAY
document_metadata.summary: The pastor reflects on his hope that his daughter Marie had matured enough to no longer need the white ribbon's moral guidance, but she collapses upon hearing his words, undermining his belief in her and the community's values.

entities.name: Children brawl and cause chaos in classroom after lesson ends
entities.description: After the lesson concludes, the children engage in chaotic behavior, including brawling, throwing sponges and chalk, and packing up their belongings in preparation to leave the classroom.

entities.name: Marie stands at classroom door acting as lookout
entities.description: Marie positions herself at the classroom door to monitor the corridor, apparently assigned to warn her classmates of any approaching teacher.

entities.name: Marie rushes into classroom and warns classmates
entities.description: Upon seeing the schoolteacher and her father approaching, Marie bursts into the classroom, closes the door to reduce noise, and shouts warnings to her classmates about the teacher's arrival.

entities.description: As the noise subsides, one child picks up a sponge and quickly wipes the blackboard clean of evidence from the earlier fight.

entities.name: Marie repeatedly shouts to quiet down the remaining noisy children
entities.description: When a group of children continues chasing each other and ignores her initial warning, Marie yells increasingly loudly at them to be quiet, culminating in a final desperate shout.

entities.name: Pastor and schoolteacher enter classroom and restore order
entities.description: The pastor and schoolteacher enter the classroom, causing immediate silence among the children due to their authoritative presence.

entities.name: Pastor drags Marie by the ear to stand facing the wall
entities.description: Without speaking, the pastor grabs Marie by the ear, drags her across the classroom, and forces her to stand facing the wall near the stove as punishment.

entities.name: Schoolteacher reprimands children for lingering and lack of discipline
entities.description: The schoolteacher, feeling responsible for the disorder, demands to know why the children are still present and reminds them that confirmation class is about to begin.

entities.name: Children quickly leave classroom after being dismissed
entities.description: The children rush to exit the classroom upon being told to leave, with one attempting to sneak out unnoticed.

entities.name: Children say goodbye to schoolteacher and pastor when prompted
entities.description: After being reminded to be polite, all the departing children call out goodbyes to both the schoolteacher and the pastor.

relations.subject: Schoolteacher
relations.description: The schoolteacher is the narrator, as revealed by the narrative voice stating 'I went to see the steward...', indicating first-person narration. However, within the scene, the schoolteacher does not directly speak to the narrator as a separate character. Instead, the narration is internal. Since the only direct speech from the schoolteacher is directed toward Liesl and the steward's wife, and no explicit dialogue occurs between the schoolteacher and a separate narrator entity, the 'is_a' relation is invalid. But given that the narrator explicitly identifies the schoolteacher as himself ('I went to see the steward...'), the most accurate allowed relation is 'speaks_to' in a momentary sense through narrative self-reference, though no direct quotation is addressed to 'the narrator' as an external entity. Given the constraint that 'speaks_to' requires directed speech with content, and no such interaction exists between schoolteacher and a distinct narrator, the relation cannot be validly rewritten. Therefore, despite the identity, no allowed relation fits without violating grounding rules.

document_metadata.title: 72 VILLAGE STREET. EXT/DUSK
document_metadata.summary: The schoolteacher grows suspicious about Hansi's disappearance, revisits the midwife's shuttered house, finds no one, and heads to the doctor's, which is also closed, deepening his concern over their unexplained absence.
